Our method begins with a global Thin Plate Spline initialization from sparse correspondences, followed by superpixel-guided segmentation that partitions the image into structurally consistent patches preserving terrain integrity. Each patch is then refined by a pretrained SynthMorph network in an unsupervised manner, enabling dense and flexible alignment without task-specific training. Finally, a fusion strategy integrates both global and local deformations into a smooth, unified deformation field. Extensive quantitative and visual evaluations demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art rigid, classical non-rigid, and learning-based methods in accuracy, structural consistency, and deformation smoothness on the challenging sonar dataset.

title: MGCR-Net: Multimodal Graph-Conditioned Vision-Language Reconstruction Network for Remote Sensing Change Detection
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: With the advancement of remote sensing satellite technology and the rapid progress of deep learning, remote sensing change detection (RSCD) has become a key technique for regional monitoring. Traditional change detection (CD) methods and deep learning-based approaches have made significant contributions to change analysis and detection, however, many outstanding methods still face limitations in the exploration and application of multimodal data. To address this, we propose the multimodal graph-conditioned vision-language reconstruction network (MGCR-Net) to further explore the semantic interaction capabilities of multimodal data. Multimodal large language models (MLLM) have attracted widespread attention for their outstanding performance in computer vision, particularly due to their powerful visual-language understanding and dialogic interaction capabilities. Specifically, we design a MLLM-based optimization strategy to generate multimodal textual data from the original CD images, which serve as textual input to MGCR. Visual and textual features are extracted through a dual encoder framework. For the first time in the RSCD task, we introduce a multimodal graph-conditioned vision-language reconstruction mechanism, which is integrated with graph attention to construct a semantic graph-conditioned reconstruction module (SGCM), this module generates vision-language (VL) Tokens through graph-based conditions and enables cross-dimensional interaction between visual and textual features via multihead attention. The reconstructed VL features are then deeply fused using the language vision transformer (LViT), achieving fine-grained feature alignment and high-level semantic interaction. Experimental results on four public datasets demonstrate that MGCR achieves superior performance compared to mainstream CD methods. Our code is available on https://github.com/cn-xvkong/MGCR.

title: GL-DT: Multi-UAV Detection and Tracking With Global–Local Integration
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: The extensive application of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in military reconnaissance, environmental monitoring, and related domains has created an urgent need for accurate and efficient multi-object tracking (MOT) technologies, which are also essential for UAV situational awareness. However, complex backgrounds, small-scale targets, and frequent occlusions and interactions continue to challenge existing methods in terms of detection accuracy and trajectory continuity. To address these issues, this paper proposes the Global-Local Detection and Tracking (GL-DT) framework. It employs a Spatio-Temporal Feature Fusion (STFF) module to jointly model motion and appearance features, combined with a global-local collaborative detection strategy, effectively enhancing small-target detection. Building upon this, the JPTrack tracking algorithm is introduced to mitigate common issues such as ID switches and trajectory fragmentation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly improves the continuity and stability of MOT while maintaining real-time performance, providing strong support for the advancement of UAV detection and tracking technologies.

title: Are Deep Learning Models Trained on Synthetic Data Actually Reliable in InSAR? A Self-Supervised Learning Approach for InSAR Phase Denoising
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Deep learning is revolutionizing the way InSAR data are processed. Supervised deep learning models trained on synthetic datasets have demonstrated strong performance according to conventional evaluation metrics. However, in practice, many supervised InSAR phase denoising filters tend to oversmooth fringe patterns and generate ghost fringes in decorrelated regions, raising concerns about the reliability of models trained solely on synthetic data in real-world applications. In this work, we introduce Noise2Fringe, an unsupervised learning framework that enables the direct training of denoising filters on noisy interferograms, eliminating the need for clean references, while achieving performance comparable to that of supervised models. This framework allows a fair comparison between models trained exclusively on real versus synthetic data, independent of the training scheme. On synthetic benchmarks, models trained on real data appear to underperform compared to those trained on synthetic data. However, in real-world interferograms, the opposite holds: synthetic-trained models oversmooth and generate ghost fringes, whereas real-trained models avoid these artifacts. These findings reveal (i) a much larger gap between synthetic and real data than previously assumed, (ii) an overestimation of the effectiveness of synthetic-trained models, and (iii) deficiencies in current evaluation methods that rely heavily on simulated benchmarks. We further find that incorporating auxiliary information, such as the Amplitude Dispersion Index, into the input can enhance denoising performance. Overall, this study demonstrates that models trained solely on synthetic data may be far less reliable in real-world applications than suggested by their benchmark results, and emphasizes that generating more realistic training datasets should take precedence over designing increasingly complex model architectures.

title: Deep Imbalanced Multitarget Regression: 3-D Point Cloud Voxel Content Estimation in Simulated Forests
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Voxelization is an effective approach to reduce the computational cost of processing Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) data, yet it results in a loss of fine-scale structural information. This study explores whether low-level voxel content information, specifically target occupancy percentage within a voxel, can be inferred from high-level voxelized LiDAR point cloud data collected from Digital Imaging and remote Sensing Image Generation (DIRSIG) software. In our study, the targets include bark, leaf, soil, and miscellaneous materials. We propose a multi-target regression approach in the context of imbalanced learning using Kernel Point Convolutions (KPConv). Our research leverages cost-sensitive learning to address class imbalance called density-based relevance (DBR). We employ weighted Mean Saquared Erorr (MSE), Focal Regression (FocalR), and regularization to improve the optimization of KPConv. This study performs a sensitivity analysis on the voxel size (0.25 - 2 meters) to evaluate the effect of various grid representations in capturing the nuances of the forest. This sensitivity analysis reveals that larger voxel sizes (e.g., 2 meters) result in lower errors due to reduced variability, while smaller voxel sizes (e.g., 0.25 or 0.5 meter) exhibit higher errors, particularly within the canopy, where variability is greatest. For bark and leaf targets, error values at smaller voxel size datasets (0.25 and 0.5 meter) were significantly higher than those in larger voxel size datasets (2 meters), highlighting the difficulty in accurately estimating within-canopy voxel content at fine resolutions. This suggests that the choice of voxel size is application-dependent. Our work fills the gap in deep imbalance learning models for multi-target regression and simulated datasets for 3D LiDAR point clouds of forests.

title: RS-MTDF: Multiteacher Distillation and Fusion for Remote Sensing Semi-Supervised Semantic Segmentation
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Semantic segmentation in remote sensing images is crucial for various applications, yet its performance is heavily reliant on large-scale, high-quality pixel-wise annotations, which are notoriously expensive and time-consuming to acquire. Semi-supervised semantic segmentation (SSS) offers a promising alternative to mitigate this data dependency. However, existing SSS methods often struggle with the inherent distribution mismatch between limited labeled data and abundant unlabeled data, leading to suboptimal generalization. To alleviate this issue, we attempt to introduce the Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) pretrained on vast and diverse datasets into the SSS task since VFMs possess robust generalization capabilities that can effectively bridge this distribution gap and provide strong semantic priors for SSS. Inspired by this, we introduce RS-MTDF (Multi-Teacher Distillation and Fusion), a novel framework that leverages the powerful semantic knowledge embedded in VFMs to guide semi-supervised learning in remote sensing. Specifically, RS-MTDF employs multiple frozen VFMs (e.g., DINOv2 and CLIP) as expert teachers, utilizing feature-level distillation to align student features with their robust representations. To further enhance discriminative power, the distilled knowledge is seamlessly fused into the student decoder. Extensive experiments on three challenging remote sensing datasets (ISPRS Potsdam, LoveDA, and DeepGlobe) demonstrate that RS-MTDF achieves state-of-the-art or comparable performance. Notably, our method outperforms existing approaches across various label ratios on LoveDA and secures the highest IoU in the majority of semantic categories. These results underscore the efficacy of multi-teacher VFM guidance in significantly enhancing both generalization and semantic understanding for remote sensing segmentation. Ablation studies further validate the contribution of each proposed module. Code is available at https://github.com/earth-insights/RS-MTDF.

title: Compress–Align–Detect: Onboard Change Detection From Unregistered Images
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Change detection from satellite images typically incurs a delay ranging from several hours up to days because of latency in downlinking the acquired images and generating orthorectified image products at the ground stations; this may preclude real or near real-time applications. To overcome this limitation, we propose shifting the entire change detection workflow onboard satellites. This requires simultaneously solving challenges in data storage, image registration, and change detection with a strict complexity constraint. In this paper, we present a novel and efficient framework for onboard change detection that addresses the aforementioned challenges in an end-to-end fashion with a deep neural network composed of three interlinked submodules: (1) image compression, tailored to minimize onboard data storage resources; (2) lightweight co-registration of non-orthorectified multi-temporal image pairs; and (3) a novel temporally invariant and computationally efficient change detection model. This is the first approach in the literature combining all these tasks in a single end-to-end framework under the constraints dictated by onboard processing. Experimental results compare each submodule with the current state of the art and evaluate the performance of the overall integrated system in a realistic setting on low-power hardware. Compelling change detection results are obtained in terms of F1-score as a function of compression rate, sustaining a throughput of 0.7 Mpixel/s on a 15 W accelerator.

title: Neural Network Model Tree Prediction for Passive Microwave Sensor Quality Control
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Earth remote sensing algorithms for spaceborne passive microwave sensors depend on high quality observations of top-of-atmosphere radiances. When these observations are adversely affected by non-geophysical processes, such as radio frequency interference (RFI), calibration drifts, or sensor anomalies, they can have detrimental impacts on retrievals or their assimilation into models. The rise of machine learning applications has exacerbated this problem because non-linear schemes can reveal even small issues with the data. A simple and computationally inexpensive method is presented for assessing the quality of observations both instantaneously and over time using a fully connected neural network model tree. The basic premise of this scheme involves using n-1 channels to predict the nth channel, and then identifying when the prediction error is larger than normal in order to identify potentially anomalous observations. Prediction error thresholds are chosen based on the application, and well-trained models with high correlations between channels can have prediction errors on the order of the noise-equivalent differential temperature (NEDT) of the sensor (less than 1 K in most cases). We find that this method is effective for identifying various types of observational problems and present case studies to this effect that demonstrate radio frequency interference, sensor electronic and physical anomalies, sun glint, and channel performance degradation. We also find that its sensitivity is ideal for quality control, even when the observational data has previously passed operational quality checks, and that this tool can be used to effectively prescreen problematic observations that may not be initially identifiable in the data application. This tool is readily available to the remote sensing community through freely distributed code with examples on training and application via a link provided in the Data Availability statement of this article.

title: Transformer-Based Inverse Radiance Transfer Framework for Global Carbon Monoxide Retrieval Using Metop-B/IASI
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Carbon monoxide (CO) plays a significant role in both climate and atmospheric chemistry by modulating hydroxyl radical concentrations. Accurate and timely global monitoring of CO concentrations is therefore crucial for assessing its climatic and environmental impacts. This study proposes a transformer-based approach called inverse radiative transfer transformer (IRTT) for retrieving global CO concentrations from Level-1C radiance data acquired by the infrared atmospheric sounding interferometer (IASI) instruments aboard Metop-B satellite. We developed an encoder-only transformer to establish the mapping between radiance and CO columns using a dataset simulated by a radiative transfer model (RTM), achieving a coefficient of determination (R2) greater than 0.999 on the validation set. The proposed model was subsequently applied to IASI-observed spectra to derive global CO vertical column densities (VCDs) from January to December 2022. Compared with the IASI products, the retrieved annual mean CO VCDs yield a correlation coefficient (R) of 0.963. In four representative regions, the model achieves high R values exceeding 0.85 with relative biases ranging from 2.42% to 6.57%. Compared with network for the detection of atmospheric composition change (NDACC) FTIR observations, IRTT yields correlation coefficients ranging from 0.77 to 0.96 across five sites with sufficient data coverage. Across 20 total carbon column observing network (TCCON) sites with sufficient data, IRTT achieves R values ranging from 0.72 to 0.94. These results are consistent with those obtained from the official Level-2 products. The model also offers high computational efficiency, requiring only ~10 s per orbit. The proposed approach shows strong potential for extension to other trace gases and satellite missions.

title: An Efficient Methodology for Viscoelastic Reverse Time Migration Based on the Finite-Difference Approach
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Amplitude decay and velocity dispersion induced by the viscous properties of subsurface formations significantly affect the energy and waveform distributions, thereby reducing the imaging quality of subsurface structures, particularly in deep and large-offset layers. Therefore, tailored absorption-attenuation compensation within viscoelastic reverse-time migration (ERTM) is pivotal for boosting imaging quality in viscoelastic subsurface media. Conventional techniques are based on the fractional-order Laplacian viscoelastic wave equation of the constant Q (CQ) model, which decouples the amplitude-decay and velocity-dispersion components. Nonetheless, the incorporation of fractional-order Laplace operators necessitates computationally intensive spectral-based methods, resulting in diminished efficiency and increased memory usage in large-scale, 3-D data processing, thereby constraining their industrial applicability. Based on the generated standard linear solid (GSLS) model, this article proposes a novel isotropic viscoelastic wave equation suitable for the ERTM. This equation decouples the amplitude decay and velocity-dispersion components and can be numerically solved using the finite difference method (FDM). Compared with the spectral methods employed in traditional CQ models, this approach offers significantly improved computational efficiency and can be readily extended to multiple SLS units. Furthermore, the method more accurately describes the attenuation behavior of the approximate CQ (ACQ) model. The ERTM algorithm, based on this equation and incorporating an attenuation-compensation mechanism, has been validated using a three-layer model and the Marmousi model. The algorithm performs exceptionally well in enhancing deep, weak reflections and improving the clarity of stratigraphic boundaries, providing a more engineering-feasible solution for seismic imaging in complex media.

title: Toward Comprehensive Interactive Change Understanding in Remote Sensing: A Large-Scale Dataset and Dual-Granularity Enhanced VLM
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Remote sensing change understanding (RSCU) is essential for analyzing remote sensing images and understanding how human activities affect the environment. However, existing datasets lack deep understanding and interactions in the diverse change captioning, counting, and localization tasks. To tackle these gaps, we construct ChangeIMTI, a new large-scale interactive multi-task instruction dataset that encompasses four complementary tasks including change captioning, binary change classification, change counting, and change localization. Building upon this new dataset, we further design a novel vision-guided vision-language model (ChangeVG) with dual-granularity awareness for bi-temporal remote sensing images (i.e., two remote sensing images of the same area at different times). The introduced visionguided module is a dual-branch architecture that synergistically combines fine-grained spatial feature extraction with high-level semantic summarization. These enriched representations further serve as the auxiliary prompts to guide large vision-language models (VLMs) (e.g., Qwen2.5-VL-7B) during instruction tuning, thereby facilitating the hierarchical cross-modal learning. We extensively conduct experiments across four tasks to demonstrate the superiority of our approach. Remarkably, on the change captioning task, our method outperforms the strongest method Semantic-CC by 1.39 points on the comprehensiveS∗mmetric, which integrates the semantic similarity and descriptive accuracy to provide an overall evaluation of change caption. Moreover, we also perform a series of ablation studies to examine the critical components of our method. The source code and associated data for this work are publicly available at Github.

title: FSFNet: Frequency–Spatial-Domain Fusion Network for Infrared Small Target Detection
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Infrared small target detection (IRSTD) is inherently challenging due to the weak feature representation of small targets and significant interference caused by complex backgrounds. Recent mainstream IRSTD methods predominantly emphasize feature extraction in the spatial domain but often neglect crucial complementary information contained in the frequency domain, resulting in limited detection performance. To address this issue, we propose a novel Frequency-Spatial Fusion Network (FSFNet), which explicitly integrates spatial-domain features and frequency-domain information through two innovative modules: the Frequency-Spatial Block (FSBlock) and the Frequency-Spatial Feature Fusion Module (FSFFM). Specifically, the FSBlock, equipped with a Spectral Band Gate (SBG) module, selectively emphasizes informative spectral bands to capture global contextual patterns and periodic characteristics in the frequency domain, thereby complementing traditional spatial-domain local representations and enhancing the network’s ability to distinguish small targets from cluttered backgrounds. Furthermore, the FSFFM adaptively combines these multi-domain features via a frequency-guided cross-channel attention mechanism, effectively bridging the semantic gap between the spatial and frequency domains. Extensive experimental evaluations on three publicly benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed FSFNet consistently achieves superior detection accuracy and robustness compared with state-of-the-art methods.

title: UAGLNet: Uncertainty-Aggregated Global–Local Fusion Network With Cooperative CNN–Transformer for Building Extraction
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Building extraction from remote sensing images is a challenging task due to the complex structure variations of the buildings. Existing methods employ convolutional or self-attention blocks to capture the multi-scale features in the segmentation models, while the inherent gap of the feature pyramids and insufficient global-local feature integration leads to inaccurate, ambiguous extraction results. To address this issue, in this paper, we present an Uncertainty-Aggregated Global-Local Fusion Network (UAGLNet), which is capable to exploit high-quality global-local visual semantics under the guidance of uncertainty modeling. Specifically, we propose a novel cooperative encoder, which adopts hybrid CNN and transformer layers at different stages to capture the local and global visual semantics, respectively. An intermediate cooperative interaction block (CIB) is designed to narrow the gap between the local and global features when the network becomes deeper. Afterwards, we propose a Global-Local Fusion (GLF) module to complementarily fuse the global and local representations. Moreover, to mitigate the segmentation ambiguity in uncertain regions, we propose an Uncertainty-Aggregated Decoder (UAD) to explicitly estimate the pixel-wise uncertainty to enhance the segmentation accuracy. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance to other state-of-the-art methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/Dstate/UAGLNet.

title: Enhancing Surface Current Retrieval From Sequential Imagery With Multiscale Deep Learning
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Accurate retrieval of ocean surface currents from sequential satellite imagery is crucial for advancing our understanding of upper-ocean dynamics and their role in climate variability. In this study, we propose CN-RAFT, a novel deep learning framework that integrates a multi-scale coarse-to-fine optical flow strategy based on the ConvNeXt architecture and Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms (RAFT), to enhance surface current estimation from sequential sea surface temperature (SST) observations. The performance of CN-RAFT is rigorously evaluated against two benchmark methods: the RAFT optical flow model and the correlation-based Window Deformation Iterative Multigrid (WIDIM) technique, using high-resolution SST and surface velocity fields from the MITgcm simulation. CN-RAFT consistently outperforms the benchmark methods, achieving lower root-mean-square error (0.9). Sensitivity experiments further demonstrate its robustness under varying spatial resolutions and noise conditions. When applied to real Himawari-9 SST data in the Kuroshio Extension, CN-RAFT successfully resolves fine-scale eddies and frontal meanders, exhibiting superior agreement with SST gradient structures. Our findings highlight CN-RAFT’s potential as an effective tool for high-resolution, real-time ocean surface current monitoring from satellite observations.

title: DA-GAN: Dual-Attention GAN for Underwater Image Enhancement With Contrast and Color Correction
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Underwater images typically suffer from severe color distortion, low contrast, and poor visibility due to light absorption and scattering in aquatic environments. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Dual-Attention GAN (DA-GAN), specifically designed to enhance contrast and correct color distortions in underwater images. DA-GAN features three key innovations: a Hybrid CNN-Attention Bottleneck Layer (HCABL) for efficient enhancement of local and global features, a Transformer-based Channel Attention Module (TCAM) for color distortion removal, and a Multi-Color Space Loss function to improve contrast and visibility. HCABL employs parallel attention mechanisms and depth-wise separable convolutions to enhance both global context and local spatial details. TCAM enhances the model’s sensitivity to various color channels, enabling effective correction of complex color distortions. Furthermore, the Multi-Color Space Loss function, tailored for the HSV color space and the image’s bright and dark channels, further enhance contrast and visibility. Comprehensive ablation studies validate the effectiveness of each component, while extensive comparison experiments demonstrate that DA-GAN achieves state-of-the-art or comparable performance across six public underwater image datasets (SUIM, UIEB, EUVP, LSUI, UCCS and SQUID). The source code is publicly available at https: //github.com/littlebearRedgood/DAGAN.

title: A Correction Methodology for Cross-Track Instrument Biases in Airborne Hyperspectral Thermal Infrared Data Over the Cryosphere
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: The Hyperspectral Thermal Emission Spectrometer (HyTES) is an airborne sensor measuring surface-leaving thermal infrared radiation (TIR) with 256 bands in the 7.5-12 µm spectral range. During its 2023 deployment over the Swiss Alps, as part of a large European campaign, instrument-related crosstrack radiometric biases were identified. We present a correction methodology tailored to glaciers. The method exploits physically constrained radiance over melting ice to derive wavelength-and pixel-specific correction factors. Developed on one flightline and applied on all six HyTES flightlines, the correction successfully reduced cross-track inconsistencies and striping artifacts. Validation with in-situ data results in a mean absolute deviation of 1.75 K, which improved by 5.3 K compared to the uncorrected data. The method can also be applied to other homogeneous surfaces, such as open water bodies or bare sand, and the corrected dataset provides unprecedented opportunities for glacier studies.

title: PhysDNet: Physics-Guided Decomposition Network of Side-Scan Sonar Imagery
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Robust matching of side-scan sonar imagery remains a fundamental challenge in seafloor mapping due to view-dependent backscatter, shadows, and geometric distortion. This paper proposes a novel matching framework that combines physical decoupling and geometric consistency to enhance correspondence accuracy and consistency across viewpoints. A multi-branch network, derived from the Lambertian reflection model, decomposes raw sonar images into seabed reflectivity, terrain elevation, and acoustic path loss. The reflectivity map, serving as a stable matching domain, is used in conjunction with a training-free matching pipeline combining SuperPoint and MINIMA-LightGlue. Geometry-aware outlier rejection leverages both terrain elevation and its physically derived shadow map to further remove mismatches in acoustically occluded and topographically inconsistent regions, thereby improving registration accuracy. Quantitative and visual evaluations against traditional, CNN-, and Transformer-based state-of-the-art methods demonstrate that our method achieves lower matching error, higher geometric consistency, and greater robustness to viewpoint variations. The proposed approach provides a data-efficient, physically interpretable solution for high-precision side-scan sonar image matching in complex seafloor environments.

title: Physics-Informed Spectral Modeling for Hyperspectral Imaging
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: We present PhISM, a physics-informed deep learning architecture that learns without supervision to explicitly disentangle hyperspectral observations and model them with continuous basis functions. PhISM outperforms previous methods on several classification and regression benchmarks, requires limited labeled data, and provides additional insights thanks to its interpretable latent representation.

title: Unified Single/Dual-Frequency PolSAR Land-Cover Segmentation via Single Model With Masked Frequency Training
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Dual-frequency (DF) Polarimetric Synthetic Aperture Radar (PolSAR) is crucial for Earth observation, offering richer information than single-frequency (SF) systems for land cover segmentation. However, SF tasks remain prevalent, and current deep learning methods typically require separate models for SF/DF tasks, hindering feature reuse across bands and broader applicability. To overcome this limitation, this letter proposes a unified network with training strategy capable of processing both SF and DF PolSAR images. Leveraging the high spatial similarity yet distinct polarimetric characteristics of DF PolSAR images, the architecture employs a shared backbone consisting of Large Kernel Selective (LKS) for joint feature extraction and Lightweight Band-specific Mixture of Experts (LBME) for capturing distinct patterns across bands. The Decoder employs Mixing Feature Transformer (MFT) blocks to refine fusion features by cross-attention and maintains robustness for SF features by explicit prompts. The proposed unified model achieves higher metrics on both SF (mIoU: 72.58% for L-band, 72.74% for S-band) and DF (mIoU: 75.19% for LS combined) tasks. The code will be made publicly available at URL

title: Map-Guided Cross-Training for Building Detection
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Extraction of building footprints from freely available, high temporal resolution satellite imagery is important for applications ranging from disaster response to monitoring informal settlements. While Sentinel-2 is globally available, limited spatial resolution restricts the reliable detection of small or densely packed structures. We propose a novel framework that re-targets a super-resolution backbone (ESRGAN) to generate cartographic map-style outputs directly and fuses it with a semantic segmentation network through joint training. Unlike pipelines treating super-resolution and detection as sequential tasks, our approach leverages map-centric supervision, unifying enhancement and building delineation. For evaluation, we introduce the S2-BDOT-PL dataset, integrating Sentinel-2 imagery with OpenStreetMap and BDOT10k ground truth. Results demonstrate improved precision and robustness in small-building detection compared to native resolution baselines.

title: SCAFNet: A Semantic Compensated Adaptive Fusion Network for Remote Sensing Images Change Detection
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Current CNN-Transformer hybrid methods for remote sensing change detection aim to address the limitations of CNNs’ constrained receptive fields and Transformers’ local detail insensitivity. However, these methods suffer from semantic misalignment and non-adaptive fusion between the dual branches, resulting in persistent sensitivity to pseudo-changes. To address these issues, we propose SCAFNet, a Semantic Compensated Adaptive Fusion Network, featuring three core components: 1) The Semantic Compensation Module (SCM) that aligns local-global features via cross-attention to resolve spatial-semantic mismatches; 2) The CNN-Transformer Feature Adaptive Fusion (CTFAF) module improving feature integration by dynamically balancing the local details of CNN and the global context of Transformer through cross-branch attention interactions and dynamic parameterization; 3) The Change Feature Identification Module (CFIM) computing channel and spatial weights, enhancing true changes while suppressing disturbances such as seasonal variations. Experiments on CDD and WHU-CD datasets demonstrate SCAFNet’s superior robustness and accuracy, outperforming existing methods through effective feature fusion. The source code and supplementary materials will be made available at https://github.com/Gyroprime/SCAFNet.

title: GAENet: A Global Attention-Aware Enhanced Network for Remote Sensing Target Detection
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Due to the large-scale variation of targets and complex background in optical remote sensing images, existing remote sensing target detection algorithms face significant challenges. To address these issues, a global attention-aware enhanced network (GAENet) for remote sensing target detection is proposed. Firstly, the convolution and attention fusion module (CAFM) is introduced in the backbone network, which effectively combines the convolution and attention mechanism modules in feature modeling, enhancing the long-distance dependency between features and the feature expression ability of local regions. Secondly, the dynamic detection head (Dyhead) is introduced, which adaptively adjusts the attention distribution to improve the model’s perception ability for targets of different scales. Experimental results on the DIOR dataset show that the proposed method can significantly improve the detection accuracy of multi-scale targets in complex scenes, achieving state-of-the-art performance. The source code is available at https://github.com/object-detection/GAENet.

title: New Accuracy Indicators for Assessing ICESat-2 Photon Cloud Filtering in Forested Areas
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Accurate photon cloud filtering is a critical preprocessing step for deriving forest parameters from ICESat-2 data. As filtering quality directly affects the reliability of subsequent applications, selecting an appropriate filtering method for a forest area is essential. Therefore, it is necessary to objectively and accurately evaluate filtering performance before further applying ICESat-2 data. However, conventional filtering accuracy indicators such as recall, precision, and F-score often fall short in objectively reflecting filtering performance, as they do not adequately capture the preservation of ground and canopy photons, nor the resulting terrain and canopy height accuracy. To address these limitations, this study proposed four new filtering accuracy indicators tailored to forest environments: Ground Signal Retention Rate (GSRR), Ground Noise Residual Rate (GNRR), Canopy Signal Retention Rate (CSRR), and Canopy Noise Residual Rate (CNRR). These indicators enable a more detailed and application-oriented evaluation of filtering performance across both ground and canopy layers. Five commonly used filtering algorithms were assessed across six representative test datasets with varying canopy cover and terrain complexity. Experimental results show that the proposed indicators exhibit a strong and statistically significant correlation with terrain RMSE, withGSRRachieving a correlation coefficient of −0.93 and ap-value below 0.001, whereas the conventional indicators exhibit absolute correlation coefficients below 0.40 andp-values greater than 0.05.

title: FSA-SARNet: A Frequency-Guided Semantic Segmentation Network for Remote Sensing SAR Images
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image semantic segmentation is crucial for all-weather, high-precision land-cover mapping. However, existing segmentation methods have limited performance due to their inability to resist well the speckle noise inherent in SAR images and neglecting the importance of frequency domain information. In this letter, we propose FSA-SARNet, a lightweight encoder-decoder network based on Frequency-Guided Attention. The main innovations of our method are as follows: (1) We design a Log-domain Guided Denoising Module (LGDM) to denoise by transforming the multiplicative speckle noise to additive noise. (2) We design a Frequency-Guided Spatial Attention Module (FGSA) to enable frequency-domain features to guide spatial-domain feature learning. (3) We introduce dynamic upsampling for the decoder to recover feature map details. Evaluated on the FUSAR-Map and WHU-OPT-SAR datasets, our method delivers superior performance and efficiency, achieving competitive MIoU scores of 42.67% and 47.00% with a compact model size of only 7.03M parameters.

title: DEM Super-Resolution Using Frequency-Selective Cross Attention Assisted by Remote Sensing Images
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Digital Elevation Model (DEM) plays a crucial role in geospatial analysis. However, high-resolution DEM is often costly to acquire and has limited spatial coverage. This letter proposes a DEM super-resolution method that integrates auxiliary information from remote sensing image (RSI): dual-branch bidirectional feature guidance network (DBFGN). The proposed method adopts the Swin Transformer as the backbone and incorporates a channel-spatial joint Transformer (CSJT) module to enhance both global and local feature extraction capabilities. To effectively extract consistent texture from RSI that strongly correlates with elevation variations, we design a mutual-guided network (MGN) based on frequency-selective cross-attention (FSCA), enabling adaptive extraction and fusion of high-frequency structure. Experiments conducted on the Swiss and Vaihingen datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing DEM and general image super-resolution methods in the challenging 8× upscaling task of DEM super-resolution, achieving RMSE and MAE of 3.108 m and 1.818 m, respectively. Compared to the second-best method, our approach improves accuracy by 8.37%, validating its effectiveness in complex height reconstruction tasks.

title: Multiscale Dynamic Graph Network for Forecasting of Wind Speeds in Offshore Regions
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Accurate prediction of wind speed in offshore areas is critical to maintaining the reliability and stability of offshore wind power. However, existing graph neural network methods focus only on a single time scale and ignore potential temporal patterns. Moreover, they rely on predefined graph structures and cannot capture dynamic spatial correlations between ocean locations, which affects the representation of offshore wind speed patterns. Therefore, we introduce the Multi-Scale Dynamic Graph Network (MSDGN) to enhance wind speed forecasting accuracy in offshore regions. MSDGN introduces a network with a multi-scale pyramid structure to capture potential time-based dependencies in raw data across various scales, and infers spatial relationships between oceanic locations at specific scales through a self-adapting learning graph network. Subsequently, the proposed temporal graph network with multi-scale concurrently captures both the time-based dependencies in sequence data and the spatial relationships among oceanic locations. Finally, the model integrates a scale-wise fusion module to facilitate cooperation among various scales, further enhancing prediction accuracy. Extensive experiments on Chinese sea data show our model outperforms state-of-the-art methods in multi-node wind speed prediction.

title: FAPMNet: Flow-Aligned Prototype Memory Network for Semantic Change Detection in Remote Sensing Images
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Semantic change detection (SCD) in bi-temporal remote sensing images aims to localize and semantically classify changed regions, which is crucial for land cover monitoring and disaster assessment. Existing methods often struggle with spatial misalignment and semantic inconsistency between temporal domains. In this letter, we propose FAPMNet, a Flow-Aligned Prototype Memory Network, which integrates a Mamba-based Vision State Space Model (VSSM) encoder for efficient long-range spatial modeling. To address temporal misalignment, a Flow Alignment Module (FAM) estimates dense flow fields to warp and align features. A Prototype Memory Module (PMM) further enhances semantic consistency via class-guided feature reconstruction. Evaluated on the SECOND and Landsat-SCD datasets, FAPMNet achieves new state-of-the-art results with 74.48% mIoU and 66.04%Fscdon SECOND, and 90.04% mIoU and 90.20%Fscdon Landsat-SCD, surpassing recent Transformer and Mamba-based baselines.

title: DCFI-Net: Dual-Branch Cross-Frequency Interaction Diffusion Model for Remote Sensing Image Shadow Removal
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Diffusion-based shadow removal methods have demonstrated impressive results on natural images, but face challenges such as high computational cost and content distortion when dealing with remote sensing images. To address these limitations, a dual-branch cross-frequency interaction diffusion model DCFI-Net for shadow removal in remote sensing images is proposed. In DCFI-Net, the diffusion process is transferred to the wavelet domain to reduce computational cost. Within the wavelet-based diffusion framework, two parallel dedicated branches for the low-frequency (LF) and high-frequency (HF) components are proposed. Then, a cross-frequency interaction module (CFIM) is utilized to facilitate the information exchange between these two branches, which guides the synergistic network optimization. Finally, we propose a feature preserving module (FPM) to mitigate the scene discrepancies between the shadow and shadow-free images. The experimental results conducted on the UAV-SC and SRGTA datasets demonstrate that DCFI-Net significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both the reconstruction and perceptual quality. Notably, DCFI-Net exhibits substantial advantages in precisely reconstructing edge details and preserving scene consistency, which are crucial for remote sensing image analysis.

title: Acoustic-to-Seismic Signal Attenuation and Aircraft Trajectory Tracking
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Airborne sound sources generate strong pressure disturbances that couple with the ground to produce acoustic-to-seismic signals, leaving a continuous seismic footprint detectable by sensors. This study simulates the seismic response of moving aircraft using the Finite Difference Method and analyzes the relationship between signal amplitude and the distance to the flight path. By integrating the wavefront diffusion equation with the distance formula, we derive a mathematical link between maximum amplitude and trajectory parameters. Based on this relation, an inversion algorithm using linear array data is developed for trajectory tracking. Field data from Beijing Capital International Airport validate the feasibility of the method. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach enables reliable large-scale and long-term aircraft monitoring, complementing traditional radar and acoustic technologies for aviation surveillance.

title: FGANet: Fuzzy-Embedded Semantic Decoupling Network for Sea–Land Segmentation in Remote Sensing Images
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Sea-Land Segmentation (SLS) of remote sensing imagery plays a vital role in coastal change analysis, intelligent ocean development, and marine resource management. However, it still faces numerous challenges, such as the difficulty in segmenting narrow waterways, spectral similarity between land and sea, and uncertainty in sea-land boundaries. To effectively overcome these challenges, we propose a fuzzy-embedded semantic information decoupling network (FGANet). First, we design a contrast-driven fusion module (CDFA) that guides multi-level feature fusion through decoupled deep features, enabling precise sea-land discrimination. Second, we develop a global prior guided fusion module (GPM) to reduce misclassification in spectrally similar regions. Finally, we introduce a fuzzy connection (FC) unit that mitigates uncertainty at the sea-land boundary through a two-dimensional Gaussian blurring approach. Comprehensive experiments are conducted on publicly available SLSD and SLBD datasets, with results confirming that the proposed FGANet outperforms other advanced existing approaches in the field.

title: A Practical Landsat-9 Land Surface Temperature Sharpen Method Combining Top-of-Atmosphere Multispectral and Panchromatic Reflectance
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: The thermal infrared (TIR) band of the Landsat-9 satellite has a spatial resolution of 100 meters, which is coarser than the optical multispectral bands of the 30-meter resolution and the panchromatic band of the 15-meter resolution. Existing image fusion algorithm studies primarily focuses on multispectral and panchromatic bands. For the TIR band with the lowest spatial resolution, although Landsat-9 land surface temperature (LST) products are resampled to 30m using the Cubic algorithm to match the multispectral bands, the physical mechanism of sharpening methods remains unclear, and they fail to fully leverage the higher spatial resolution advantage provided by the panchromatic band. This study proposes a practical LST sharpening method (TOA-MsPS) by integrating the correlation between top-of-atmosphere TIR brightness temperature (BT) and the fused reflectance of Multispectral and Panchromatic bands. The TOA-MsPS method comprises three steps: panchromatic and multispectral band fusion, correlation modeling of reflectance and BT, and LST end-to-end retrieval. Compared to existing methods, the TOA-MsPS method sharpens the spatial resolution of both TIR band BT images to 15 m without relying on external parameters, simultaneously deriving the LST data. All input data for the method consists of remote sensing observations at the TOA, reducing external parameter uncertainties and error propagation inherent in the preprocessing steps of current LST retrieval algorithms, such as atmospheric correction, resampling, and emissivity estimation. Qualitative visual interpretation based on visual inspection indicate that TOA-MsPS derived LST images exhibit significantly enhanced detail and reasonable local spatial distribution. Quantitative validations using ground site measurements demonstrate that the sharpened LST images achieve comparable accuracy to Landsat-9 LST products while substantially improving spatial resolution, with root mean square errors of 2.45K (LST product) and 2.35K (LST sharpen), respectively. Furthermore, the TOA-MsPS method can be directly applied to remote sensing data from multiple other remote sensing data sources, further enhancing the precision of long-term land surface thermal radiance monitoring.

title: Spatial-Frequency Joint Learning Mamba for Hyperspectral Image Classification
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification, as a crucial research direction in remote sensing, aims to achieve pixel-wise land cover classification by leveraging the abundant spectral and spatial information of HSI. However, existing approaches direct their primary attention to spectral-spatial feature analysis while neglecting to explore latent properties in the frequency domain. To solve this issue, we put forward a spatial-frequency joint learning Mamba (SFMamba) framework for HSI classification. Its core component is the Wavelet Mamba Block (WMB), which adopts a dual-branch design with spatial and frequency branches. In the spatial branch, we utilize convolutional layers for spatial domain feature extraction. In the frequency branch, we use wavelet transform to decompose input features into a low-frequency component together with three high-frequency components. The low-frequency component is processed by a convolutional block, while the high-frequency components are modeled by a Mamba block, achieving effective learning of both local and global representations in the frequency domain. Experimental results on two public datasets show that SFMamba outperforms several existing classification methods, demonstrating its effectiveness. Specifically, SFMamba achieves overall accuracies of 98.92% on the ZY1-02D Huanghekou (ZYHHK) dataset and 99.03% on the WHU-Hi-LongKou (LongKou) dataset. Our code is available at: https://github.com/zhe-meng/SFMamba.

title: Improving the Spatial Representation of Reservoir Evaporation Using SAR-Based Wind Fields
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Evaporation losses from reservoirs can be substantial, yet spatial variability in evaporation rates is difficult to quantify, in part due to the difficulty of estimating high-resolution wind fields at the water-air interface. Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) offers a promising approach to estimate high-resolution wind fields over lakes. To test the utility of SAR-based winds to improve spatial representation of reservoir evaporation, we developed a framework fusing Sentinel-1 based wind fields with gridded meteorological estimates of air temperature, humidity, and solar radiation to estimate distributed evaporation rates at Lake Mead, USA using the Penman open water evaporation equation. We validated outputs at over-water buoys and benchmarked the results against wind and evaporation estimates derived solely from the Real-Time Mesoscale Analysis (RTMA) data product. Sentinel-1 wind field accuracy matched or outperformed RTMA, with a wind direction mean absolute error (MAE) of 41.3° compared to 40.3° and a wind speed MAE of 1.3 m/s compared to 1.8 m/s. This framework yielded a 25x increase in spatial resolution of wind fields (100 m) and evaporation (100 m) compared to RTMA-alone (2500 m), enabling identification of greater spatial variability across Lake Mead than was previously possible. This framework could be used globally for high-resolution evaporation mapping to support water resources monitoring, modeling, and management.

title: Hybrid Integration of CNN and Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks for Multispectral Image Super-Resolution
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: This letter proposes KAN-MSI-SR (KMSR), a novel deep learning framework for multispectral image super-resolution that integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs). The model employs a KAN-Block to enhance nonlinear spectral-spatial representation, combined with CNNs for local feature extraction. Supported by channel weighting, residual connections, and global skip links, the approach effectively improves reconstruction accuracy and spectral consistency. Experiments on Sentinel-2 imagery demonstrate that KMSR outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative metrics and visual quality, providing a robust and efficient solution for Multispectral imagery (MSI) super-resolution.

title: Incidence Angle Optimization for Formation-Flying Across-Track SAR Interferometry
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Single-pass across-track synthetic aperture radar (SAR) interferometry using formation flying is a well-established technique for the generation of high-quality digital elevation models (DEMs), as it avoids temporal decorrelation and allows for long baselines, thus leading to high height accuracy. A successful implementation, employed in the TanDEM-X mission, foresees the use of a Helix formation, which entails a reduced control effort to be maintained in the presence of external perturbations. However, an intrinsic limitation of the Helix concept lies in the inherently time-varying baseline and height of ambiguity (HoA), which results in non-homogeneous DEM performance. This letter proposes an analytical method to minimize the HoA variability at the global level by optimizing the range of incidence angles used at each latitude. The approach is primarily aimed at systems, such as TanDEM-X, for which the area to be imaged becomes significantly smaller than the ground access range as the latitude increases. A two-step approach is presented: An initial approximate solution is derived in closed form and subsequently refined. The method is validated against numerical results and compared with simpler strategies involving fixed incidence angles, showing reduced variation of the HoA for different formation parameters. The procedure presented in this work could enable a better operation of current interferometric SAR systems and foster an improved design of future ones.

title: Relationship Between Wave-Related Reynolds Number and Doppler Velocity at Grazing Incidence
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: We show empirical evidence that the mean spatial gradient of the Doppler velocity, measured by a coherent X-band marine radar at grazing incidence, serves as a reliable proxy for measuring the so-called wave-related Reynolds number - defined as the product of air-side friction velocity and significant wave height divided by the kinematic viscosity of the surface water. Comparisons to approximately 180 hours of in situ observations spanning various environmental conditions in the Southern North Sea yield an overall squared correlation coefficient of 0.93, and a normalized root-mean-square error of 16%. These results suggest that coherent marine radar offers a practical and relatively cost-efficient tool for observing key parameters related to ocean surface dynamics and air-sea interactions, such as whitecap coverage.

title: RARM-YOLO: Remote Sensing Small-Target Detection Model Enhanced by Dual-Branch Region-Aware Refinement Module
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Remote sensing image object detection is characterized by dim features of small objects and complex backgrounds. In most networks, simply enhancing small object features may disrupt global consistency and affect detection results. This paper designs a region-aware refinement module to locate the enhanced target semantic representation and suppress background noise interference, and a dual detection branch to fuse underlying details and shallow semantic features at the neck of the feature pyramid, enhancing the model’s ability to focus on very small targets. Experimental results show that the improved model achieves an mAP50% of 76.0% on the VEDAI dataset, which is 10.6% higher than the original YOLOv8s. The mAP50-95% is 46.5%, which is 7% higher. The precision and recall rates are improved by 7.5% and 12.2% respectively. The generalization performance was verified on VisDrone2019 and SODA-A remote sensing datasets, with mAP50% of 47.1% and 73.8% respectively, a model size of only 29.5MB, balancing lightweight and high detection performance. This method provides a technical approach involving the cooperative optimisation of multiple modules for target detection in complex remote sensing scenes, offering significant application value.

title: A Multitask Collaborative Learning Approach for Fine-Grained Object Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Fine-grained object detection in remote sensing images is challenged by high intra-class variation and low inter-class distinction, as well as optimization inconsistency between classification and localization tasks. To address these, we propose MCLNet, a Multi-Task Collaborative Learning Network. MCLNet is a dual-stream architecture that integrates fine-grained classification with coarse-grained detection to improve detection accuracy. To enhance oriented localization, we treat all fine-grained objects as coarse-grained ones during training, which expands the dataset and improves the accuracy of oriented localization in the coarse-grained detection stream. Besides, we introduce a Coarse-to-Fine Hierarchical Constraint Mechanism (CHCM) that uses coarse-grained predictions as priors to guide fine-grained learning, enhancing both intra-class and inter-class feature representations. Additionally, we employ a Progressive Multi-Task Optimization Strategy (PMOS) that gradually trains the model to balance classification and localization tasks, reducing task interference. Extensive experiments on widely used benchmark datasets validate that MCLNet outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in fine-grained object detection.

title: LGRI: A Multimodal Image Registration Method Integrating Adaptive Log-Gabor Filtering With Rotation-Invariant Descriptors
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Multimodal image registration aims to accurately align images with differences in spatial structure or optical characteristics, serving as a key technology in remote sensing image processing and analysis. Currently, most registration methods are designed only for single-modal or limited cross-modal scenarios, often leading to distortions, artifacts, and registration errors when processing multimodal data. To address this issue, we propose a multimodal remote sensing image registration method called LGRI (Log-Gabor Rotation-Invariant), which integrates adaptive Log-Gabor feature extraction with rotation-invariant local binary descriptors. Specifically, we first design an adaptive Log-Gabor Structural-Frequency Detector (LGSFD) to extract highly repeatable and discriminative cross-modal feature points by leveraging spatial structure and frequency response. Then, we propose a Rotation-Invariant Noise-Robust Local Binary Descriptor (RINR-LBD), which improves robustness via arc-segment mean smoothing and ensures descriptor consistency through principal direction normalization. Finally, we refine the matches using Fast Sample Consensus (FSC) to effectively eliminate mismatches and improve registration accuracy. Experimental results show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in both the average number of correct matches and the matching success rate.

title: DA-PhysDiff: A Dual-Aware Physics-Informed Diffusion Model for SAR Image Despeckling
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Deep learning-based Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) despeckling faces two key challenges: physical model mismatch, where simplified noise assumptions fail to capture speckle’s statistics, and architectural generality, where standard networks struggle to separate noise from texture. To address this, we propose DA-PhysDiff, a dual-aware physics-informed diffusion model for SAR image despeckling. The proposed LogGamma-based stochastic differential equation models multiplicative speckle more accurately, while the dual-aware network composed of a Statistics-Conditioned Gamma Attention (SCGA) and a Frequency-Refined Adaptive Wavelet Convolution (FRA-WTConv) enhances both distribution and frequency awareness. Experiments on HRSID, MiniSAR, and synthetic benchmarks demonstrate that DA-PhysDiff achieves up to +2.5 dB PSNR and +4.8% EPD-ROA improvement over recent diffusion models, while reducing parameters by 19% compared with SAR-DDPM and maintaining real-time inference.

title: The New Technology for Soil Moisture Measurement Based on GNSS-S Radar
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Soil moisture is a key variable governing land–atmosphere water and energy exchanges. This letter proposes a novel soil moisture retrieval technique based on GNSS-S (Global Navigation Satellite System–Scattering) radar. Unlike conventional GNSS-R systems that are restricted to specular reflection points, the proposed GNSS-S radar exploits distributed GNSS backscattering to enable continuous bistatic imaging of surface soil moisture. The system is mounted on an airborne or spaceborne platform and uses navigation satellites as illuminators of opportunity. GNSS-S imaging is achieved through signal-level preprocessing, backprojection-based image formation, geometric correction, and relative radiometric calibration. Airborne experiments demonstrate that continuous surface imaging with a spatial resolution of approximately 100 m × 100 m can be achieved using L-band GNSS signals. Comparative analysis with in-situ soil moisture measurements shows consistent spatial distribution trends, and quantitative evaluation reveals moderate to strong correlations depending on bistatic geometry. These results validate the feasibility of GNSS-S radar for area-wide soil moisture monitoring and highlight its potential as a complementary technique to conventional active SAR systems.

title: Four-Component Polarimetric Decomposition Method for High-Resolution PolSAR Vehicle Targets Based on Extended Scattering Models
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Polarimetric target decomposition is fundamental for interpreting scattering mechanisms in polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) imagery. However, existing model-based methods often overestimate volume scattering, exhibit coupling between surface and double-bounce components, and yield unstable results on high-resolution airborne data, particularly for man-made vehicle targets, hindering accurate characterization. This letter proposes a novel four-component decomposition method designed for high-resolution airborne PolSAR imagery. Building upon the classical modeling of volume and helix scattering, two physically extended components are incorporated: an extended surface scattering model and an extended double-bounce scattering model. The former employs a rotated dipole to describe surface polarization anisotropy beyond ideal single-bounce assumptions, while the latter incorporates a rotated quarter-wave mechanism to characterize amplitude–phase inconsistencies neglected in conventional dihedral models. Experiments on a high-resolution Ku-band vehicle dataset demonstrate that the proposed method effectively suppresses volume overestimation, alleviates surface–double-bounce coupling, and enhances component stability while preserving edge and structural fidelity. The model achieves improved adaptability to complex targets without increasing component dimensionality, while maintaining strong physical interpretability, offering a new pathway for refined vehicle scattering analysis in airborne PolSAR data.

title: Automatic Coseismic Landslide Mapping by Integrating Classification and Change Detection Techniques
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Automatic co-seismic landslide mapping plays a crucial role in rapidly assessing post-disaster impacts and supporting emergency response efforts. However, most remote sensing-based approaches depend on either classification or change detection alone, failing to fully exploit their complementary strengths and thus limiting mapping accuracy. To address this issue, this study proposes a novel co-seismic landslide mapping approach that integrates classification and change detection techniques. The proposed approach consists of two main stages: automatic landslide sample generation and classifier-based mapping, both integrating classification and change detection. Specifically, in the first stage, sample reliability is improved by combining coarse change detection using pre- and post-event images with coarse classification based on the post-event image. In the second stage, classification and change detection results are fused using a maximum class probability decision strategy to further enhance mapping accuracy. Experiments conducted on two datasets covering the Mainling area in China and the Hokkaido region in Japan demonstrate that the proposed method achieved superior performance compared with existing approaches.

title: Unveiling Spectral Attention Redundancy With Explainable AI
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification has advanced significantly through transformer-based models that leverage self-attention (SA) to capture global spectral dependencies. However, most existing HSI transformers implicitly assume that SA provides a faithful and discriminative modeling of spectral information, an assumption that has rarely been examined. We examine SA behavior in HSI classification using adversarial perturbations guided by explainable AI (XAI) techniques. By comparing transformer attention distributions with Integrated Gradients (IG) importance scores, we uncover discrepancies between attended bands and decision-driving features. Experiments show that SA often forms redundant clusters across neighboring spectral bands and that attention patterns evolve across layers, shifting from a localized to a broader focus. Such redundancy improves robustness to spectral corruptions but reduces feature specificity and leads to repeated processing of highly similar bands, increasing computational burden. Our findings question the everyday use of raw attention as an explanatory clue and guide the design of more reliable and interpretable attention mechanisms for HSI.

title: Large-Scale Forest Height Estimation With TanDEM-X InSAR and Sparse LiDAR Based on LSC and Block Adjustment Model
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: The TanDEM-X bistatic Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) system has great potential for forest height estimation. However, single-polarization InSAR data cannot support a uniquely determined inversion of classical physical models due to insufficient observational information. Simplified models make inversion possible using only interferometric coherence amplitude, at the cost of reduced performance by uncertain semi-empirical parameters and a loss of adaptivity to variations in local forest properties. To address this issue, this letter proposes a framework based on a semi-empirical physical model, block adjustment model, and the least-squares collocation (LSC) method. The framework utilizes sparse spaceborne LiDAR canopy height as a reference and selects tie points in overlapping areas to establish constraints, enabling robust estimation of semi-empirical model parameters on a large scale. Subsequently, variance-covariance estimation is employed to develop an LSC-based local calibration method, mitigating residual inversion errors caused by variations in forest attributes and terrain slope within local areas. Validation at two test sites in the USA and Spain shows that, compared to the results obtained from the SINC model and semi-empirical model inversions, the proposed framework improves accuracy by more than 32% and 21%, respectively, highlighting its potential for large-scale forest height mapping with TanDEM-X InSAR and sparse LiDAR data.

title: UniMGS: Unsupervised Multimodal Guided Segmentation for High-Resolution Remote Sensing Images
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Generating pixel-level annotations for the semantic segmentation of high-resolution remote sensing images is labor-intensive and time-consuming. To address this issue, numerous studies attempt to generate pixel-level annotations through automatic or semi-automatic labeling strategies. However, due to the inherent complexity of remote sensing imagery and the presence of unseen classes, achieving both accurate foreground segmentation and precise class labeling remains highly challenging. In this paper, we propose an Unsupervised Multimodal Guided Segmentation (UniMGS) framework that generates pseudo-labels for remote sensing images without requiring any ground-truth annotations or additional prompts. Specifically, We propose a Mask Purification Module (MPM) that refines class-agnostic segmentation masks by applying an area filter and a ring-merging strategy to remove noisy masks and merge over-segmented regions. To assign precise categories to class-agnostic segmentation masks, we propose a Text-Driven Classifier (TDC) module. This module constructs an intra-class maximum spanning tree from a similarity matrix and incorporates cluster size constraints together with a confidence scoring mechanism, ultimately achieving precise class labeling. Experimental results on multiple remote sensing datasets demonstrate that UniMGS outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods. Our source code is available at https://github.com/nanwang0511/UniMGS.

title: Local-Motion Mamba With Frequency-Guided for Moving Infrared Small Target Detection
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Moving Infrared Small Target Detection (MISTD) remains challenging due to the large computational load caused by multi-frame input and background motion interference, leading to poor real-time and accuracy performance. To address these issues, we propose STLMamba, a spatial-temporal framework that integrates long-range dependency modeling with local feature sensitivity, guided by infrared video and frequency priors. Specifically, an Adaptive Multi-directional Frequency Enhancement (AMFE) module exploits spatial frequency cues to enhance targets, while an Efficient Local-motion Mamba (ELM) with a learnable Local Dynamic Gaussian Motion (LDGM) mechanism captures motion patterns and suppresses background noise. Experiments demonstrate that STLMamba achieves 43.14 FPS in NUDT-MIRSDT and 49.22 FPS in TSIRMT, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and efficiency.

title: DCTNet: Integrating Deformable Convolution and Transformer-Based Feature Fusion for High-Performance SAR Ship Detection
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR)–based ship detection has become an indispensable technique for applications in maritime surveillance, oceanic defense systems, and marine resource assessment. However, factors such as speckle noise, sea clutter, and the diversity of ship scales severely restrict the robustness and accuracy of detection. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a one-stage detection network, termed DCTNet, which integrates a Deformable Convolution-based Multi-scale Fusion (DCMF) module and a Transformer-enhanced Feature Pyramid Aggregation Network (TFPAN). The DCMF module employs deformable convolution and channel partitioning to adaptively capture multi-scale features, thereby enhancing the representation of small-scale or low-contrast ships while effectively suppressing background interference. The TFPAN module incorporates Transformer attention mechanisms with progressive feature aggregation to strengthen multi-scale feature interaction and semantic consistency. In addition, a Triple Feature Fusion (TFF) strategy is designed to preserve local details and ensure global context transmission, effectively mitigating the loss of small target features during the fusion process. Experimental results on the SAR-Ship-Dataset and HRSID demonstrate that the proposed DCTNet achieves excellent performance and exhibits strong generalization ability.

title: SRAW-Attack: Space-Reweighted Adversarial Warping Attack for SAR Target Recognition
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery exhibits intrinsic information sparsity due to its unique electromagnetic scattering mechanism. Despite the widespread adoption of deep neural network (DNN)-based SAR automatic target recognition (SAR-ATR) systems, they remain vulnerable to adversarial examples and tend to over-rely on background regions, leading to degraded adversarial robustness. Existing adversarial attacks for SAR-ATR often require visually perceptible distortions to achieve effective performance, thereby necessitating an attack method that balances effectiveness and stealthiness. In this paper, a novel attack method termed Space-Reweighted Adversarial Warping (SRAW) is proposed, which generates adversarial examples through optimized spatial deformation with reweighted budgets across foreground and background regions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SRAW significantly degrades the performance of state-of-the-art SAR-ATR models and consistently outperforms existing methods in terms of imperceptibility and adversarial transferability. Code is made available at https://github.com/boremycin/SAR-ATR-TransAttack.

title: Multitask GLocal OBIA-Mamba for Sentinel-2 Landcover Mapping
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Although Sentinel-2 based land use and land cover (LULC) classification is critical for various environmental monitoring applications, it is a very difficult task due to some key data challenges (e.g., spatial heterogeneity, context information, signature ambiguity). This paper presents a novel Multitask Glocal OBIA-Mamba (MSOM) for enhanced Sentinel-2 classification with the following contributions. First, an object-based image analysis (OBIA) Mamba model (OBIA-Mamba) is designed to reduce redundant computation without compromising fine-grained details by using superpixels as Mamba tokens. Second, a global-local (GLocal) dual-branch convolutional neural network (CNN)-mamba architecture is designed to jointly model local spatial detail and global contextual information. Third, a multitask optimization framework is designed to employ dual loss functions to balance local precision with global consistency. The proposed approach is tested on Sentinel-2 imagery in Alberta, Canada, in comparison with several advanced classification approaches, and the results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves higher classification accuracy and finer details that the other state-of-the-art methods.

title: AMFS-Net: An Adaptive Multiscale Feature Fusion Framework for Efficient SAR Ship Detection
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters

title: Clustering-Guided Spatial–Spectral Mamba for Hyperspectral Image Classification
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Although Mamba models greatly improve Hyperspectral Image (HSI) classification, they have critical challenges in terms defining efficient and adaptive token sequences for improve performance. This paper therefore presents CSSMamba (Clustering-guided Spatial-Spectral Mamba) framework to better address the challenges, with the following contributions. First, to achieve efficient and adaptive token sequences for improved Mamba performance, we integrate the clustering mechanism into a spatial Mamba architecture, leading to a cluster-guided spatial Mamba module (CSpaMamba) that reduces the Mamba sequence length and improves Mamba feature learning capability. Second, to improve the learning of both spatial and spectral information, we integrate the CSpaMamba module with a spectral mamba module (SpeMamba), leading to a complete clustering-guided spatial-spectral Mamba framework. Third, to further improve feature learning capability, we introduce an Attention-Driven Token Selection mechanism to optimize Mamba token sequencing. Last, to seamlessly integrate clustering into the Mamba model in a coherent manner, we design a Learnable Clustering Module that learns the cluster memberships in an adaptive manner. Experiments on the Pavia University, Indian Pines, and Liao-Ning 01 datasets demonstrate that CSSMamba achieves higher accuracy and better boundary preservation compared to state-of-the-art CNN, Transformer, and Mamba-based methods.

title: Activation Map-Based Visual Explanation for Remote Sensing Image Super-Resolution
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Deep learning has enhanced image super-resolution (SR) performance, yet SR networks are often treated as black boxes with limited explainability. Notably, remote sensing(RS) images possess explicit physical semantics, imposing stringent demands on the explainability of their SR methods. To address this, we propose AMVE-SR, a framework that systematically transfers activation map-based visual explanation (AMVE) from classification networks to SR networks. Distinct from classification-oriented methods (e.g., Grad-CAM) that struggle with shallow-layer visualization or computationally intensive perturbation-based approaches, AMVE-SR introduces a layer-wise recursive propagation mechanism. By exploiting inter-layer correlations, it traces activation maps backward to the input, ensuring high-fidelity explanations even in shallow layers where conventional methods fail to transfer effectively. Furthermore, we compute gradient responses via textural discrepancy rather than raw pixel intensities, capturing high-frequency details (e.g., physical boundaries) essential for physical semantics. To address the lack of quantitative metrics, we propose Average Texture Variation (ATV) by adapting the Average Drop concept in classification tasks. Validated by visual consistency, ATV serves as a novel fidelity metric for SR explanations. Experiments on the AID dataset using the EDSR model demonstrate that our method produces visually reliable explanation maps while achieving superior performance on the proposed ATV metric with high running efficiency. In general, this study extends AMVE from image classification to SR, thereby establishing a new paradigm to explain SR networks.

title: Evaluation of the Velocity Recovery and Dealiasing Algorithm for Dual-PRF Scans
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters

title: LaCon: Late-Constraint Controllable Visual Generation
abstract: Diffusion models have demonstrated impressive abilities in generating photo-realistic and creative images. To offer more controllability for the generation process of diffusion models, previous studies normally adopt extra modules to integrate condition signals by manipulating the intermediate features of the noise predictors, where they often fail in conditions not seen in the training. Although subsequent studies are motivated to handle multi-condition control, they are mostly resource-consuming to implement, where more generalizable and efficient solutions are expected for controllable visual generation. In this paper, we present a late-constraint controllable visual generation method, namely LaCon, which enables generalization across various modalities and granularities for each single-condition control. LaCon establishes an alignment between the external condition and specific diffusion timesteps, and guides diffusion models to produce conditional results based on this built alignment.
